card.name: Linking words before condition or symptom terms
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as of, is, be, concurrent, chronic or acute that sit right before a medical condition, such as pain, withdrawal or ototoxicity. They appear in label text about managing or treating a problem.

modes.label: Of after management or history
modes.description: The word of follows a noun like management, development or history and comes just before a condition.
modes.example: short-term (up to 5 days in adults), management<< of>> moderately severe acute pain that requires analges

modes.label: Chronic or acute before pain
modes.description: An adjective such as chronic, acute or concurrent comes before a disease or pain term.
modes.example: Patients with<< chronic>> pain should have their dosage given on an

modes.label: Is or be after a side effect
modes.description: A linking verb comes after a named adverse effect, just before a description of it.

card.writes: It seems to push the model toward words like treat, treated and marked, as in what is treated or how marked an effect is.
card.plain: It fires on small connecting words just before a condition or side effect is named or described.
